symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed integer independent of the number of clusters.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,K\}\).

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: A fixed integer independent of the number of clusters.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: The finite number of clusters in the experiment.

symbols.name: \mathcal G
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G=\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: \(s=(s_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) records every labeled cluster size.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: \(N=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}s_g\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r_{q,a}\) is the prescribed treated count in a size-\(q\) cluster assigned label \(a\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: \(c=(c_{z,a})\) fixes the person-weighted causal contrast.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y_{g i}(z,a)\) is unit \(i\)'s outcome under own treatment \(z\) and cluster saturation label \(a\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.def: The class defined in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: \(\tau(Y)=N^{-1}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\sum_{i=1}^{s_g}\sum_{z\in\{0,1\}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_{z,a}Y_{g i}(z,a)\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: \(L=\frac12\sum_{z\in\{0,1\}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}|c_{z,a}|\), so \(\tau(Y)\in[-L,L]\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X=((A_g,S_g))_{g\in\mathcal G}\) records each saturation label and its exact treated subset.

symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X\) is the set of all assignments allowed by the treated-count table \(r\).

symbols.name: \mathcal O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O(X)=\{(g,i,\mathbf 1\{i\in S_g\},A_g):g\in\mathcal G,1\le i\le s_g\}\).

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V=(Y_{g i}(\mathbf 1\{i\in S_g\},A_g))_{g,i}\), equivalently the restriction of \(Y\) to \(\mathcal O(X)\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: A probability law on the complete feasible assignment \(X\), allowing arbitrary dependence across clusters and stages.

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A possibly nonlinear and biased rule based on the full assignment and revealed outcomes, clipped to \([-L,L]\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R(D,\delta;Y)=\mathbb E_D[(\delta(X,V)-\tau(Y))^2]\), where only \(X\) is random.

symbols.name: R^\star
symbols.def: \(R^\star=\inf_{D,\delta}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R(D,\delta;Y)\).

symbols.name: \Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma\) permutes units within clusters and permutes equal-size clusters, where \(m_q=|\{g:s_g=q\}|\).

symbols.name: \mathcal K
symbols.def: Each \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\) is a size-tagged histogram of cluster response types, and each cluster response type is a multiset of complete \(2K\)-bit unit response vectors.

symbols.name: \mathcal N
symbols.def: Each \(n\in\mathcal N\) is the size-tagged histogram \((n_{q,a})\) of saturation labels.

symbols.name: \mathcal W
symbols.def: Each \(\omega\in\mathcal W\) is a size-tagged histogram of local triples \((a,u,v)\), with treated-one count \(u\) and control-one count \(v\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The table defined in \(\texttt{def:local-kernel}\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The coefficient construction in \(\texttt{def:orbit-kernel}\).

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: \(\theta_\kappa=\tau(Y)\) for any binary schedule \(Y\) in response orbit \(\kappa\).

symbols.name: \overline R
symbols.def: A directly evaluated upper certificate for \(R^\star\).

symbols.name: \underline R
symbols.def: A directly evaluated lower certificate for \(R^\star\).

symbols.name: \mathsf P
symbols.def: The perspective program in \(\texttt{def:primal-game}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf Q
symbols.def: The least-favorable-prior program in \(\texttt{def:dual-game}\).

symbols.name: R_{\mathrm{ind}}
symbols.def: \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}=\inf_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal A),\delta}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R(D_p,\delta;Y)\), where cluster labels are independent with common law \(p\) and treated subsets are conditionally independent and uniform.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: A user-specified outward-rounding tolerance.

symbols.name: \mathfrak C
symbols.def: The handle defined in \(\texttt{def:compiler-handle}\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(g\in\mathcal G\), \(1\le i\le s_g\), \(z\in\{0,1\}\), and \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(0\le Y_{g i}(z,a)\le1\).
Each \(Y_{g i}(z,a)\) depends on the realized assignment only through unit \(i\)'s own treatment \(z\) and its cluster label \(a\).

standard.name: stratified interference with anonymous saturation exposure

assumptions.condition: For every \(q\in\{3,\ldots,b\}\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(1\le r_{q,a}\le q-1\).
There exist \(g\in\mathcal G\) and distinct \(a,a'\in\mathcal A\) such that \(r_{s_g,a}\ne r_{s_g,a'}\).

definitions.name: Bounded anonymous-saturation class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{Y=(Y_{g i}(z,a)): 0\le Y_{g i}(z,a)\le1\text{ for every }(g,i,z,a),\text{ and }Y_{g i}\text{ obeys anonymous stratified interference}\}\).

definitions.name: Multilinear endpoint extension
definitions.construction: For an endpoint table \(d\), define \(\overline d(X,V)=\mathbb E[d(X,B|_{\mathcal O(X)})\mid V]\), where the revealed coordinates of \(B\) are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with means equal to the corresponding coordinates of \(V\).
inputs: an estimator table on binary observation cells

definitions.name: Local exact-count response kernel
definitions.construction: For a size-\(q\) cluster response type \(t\), set \(P_{t,a}(u,v)=\binom{q}{r_{q,a}}^{-1}\#\{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}:|S|=r_{q,a},\ \sum_{i\in S}t_{i,1,a}=u,\ \sum_{i\notin S}t_{i,0,a}=v\}\).

definitions.name: Stabilizer-weighted observation-hypergraph kernel
definitions.construction: For response histogram \(\kappa\), assignment histogram \(n\), and compatible observation histogram \(\omega\), let \(F_{\kappa,q}(z)=\prod_t(\sum_{a,u,v}P_{t,a}(u,v)z_{a,u,v})^{\kappa_{q,t}}\) and \(H_{\kappa n\omega}=\prod_{q=3}^{b}[z^{\omega_q}]F_{\kappa,q}(z)/\binom{m_q}{(n_{q,a})_{a\in\mathcal A}}\); set the entry to zero when the label margins are incompatible.

definitions.name: Closed-perspective procedure program
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf P=\min \overline R\) over \(d_n\ge0\) and \(t_{n\omega}\) subject to \(\sum_nd_n=1\), \(-Ld_n\le t_{n\omega}\le Ld_n\), and \(\sum_{n,\omega}H_{\kappa n\omega}(t_{n\omega}-d_n\theta_\kappa)^2/d_n\le \overline R\) for every \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\), using the closed quadratic perspective at \(d_n=0\).

definitions.name: Least-favorable-prior conic program
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal K)\), define \(a_{n\omega}=\sum_\kappa\pi_\kappa H_{\kappa n\omega}\), \(h_{n\omega}=\sum_\kappa\pi_\kappa H_{\kappa n\omega}\theta_\kappa\), and \(b_n=\sum_\kappa\pi_\kappa\theta_\kappa^2-\sum_\omega h_{n\omega}^2/a_{n\omega}\), with zero contribution when \(a_{n\omega}=0\); then \(\mathsf Q=\max_{\pi,\underline R}\underline R\) subject to \(\underline R\le b_n\) for every \(n\in\mathcal N\), represented by rotated-cone epigraphs.

definitions.name: Independent-saturation saddle feasibility system
definitions.construction: The system seeks \(p\in\Delta(\mathcal A)\), a clipped table \(\delta_{n\omega}\), \(\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal K)\), and \(v\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\sum_{n,\omega}d_n(p)H_{\kappa n\omega}(\delta_{n\omega}-\theta_\kappa)^2\le v\) for every \(\kappa\), and \(b_n(\pi)\ge v\) for every \(n\), where \(d_n(p)=\prod_q\binom{m_q}{(n_{q,a})_a}\prod_ap_a^{n_{q,a}}\) and \(0^0=1\).
inputs: the primal and dual orbit data

definitions.name: Bit-certified orbit-compiler handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathfrak C\) by canonical size-tagged response, assignment, and observation histograms; compute every stabilizer-weighted coefficient by bounded-alphabet dynamic programming; perform rational facial reduction for zero-mass cells; invoke weak second-order-cone optimization; outward-round and directly verify the resulting primal and dual risks; decode the continuous estimator through the Bernoulli histogram recursion from \(\texttt{def:endpoint-extension}\).

statements.statement: For every feasible treated-count table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary counts and menus constant in \(a\), every joint design \(D\in\Delta(\mathcal X)\) and measurable rule \(\delta\) can be averaged over \(\prod_{g\in\mathcal G}\mathfrak S_{s_g}\) and then conditioned on the assignment to produce a design-rule pair whose worst-case risk is no larger, whose saturation-label law may retain arbitrary cross-cluster dependence, and whose treated subset in each cluster is uniform conditional on its saturation label and independent across clusters conditional on the label vector. Consequently imposing this conditional uniformity does not change \(R^\star\).
statements.justification: This separates the substantive first-stage correlation choice from within-slice label asymmetry, including the degenerate uniform law on a unique empty or full treated subset.
statements.gap: Bai2023 proves permutation symmetrization for no-interference minimax schemes, while BasseFeller2018 assumes the standard second-stage symmetry; neither transports an unrestricted nonlinear estimator through the full saturation observation hypergraph.
statements.consumer: A saturation-experiment designer needs only implement uniform exact-count sampling within clusters after solving for the correlated first-stage law.

statements.statement: For fixed \(K\) and \(b\), every rational table satisfying \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including tables with boundary entries or a treated-count menu constant in \(a\), every rational contrast \(c\), and every size profile \(s\), \(R^\star\) is unchanged when nature is restricted to binary schedules. Every endpoint estimator table \(d\) has the multilinear extension \(\overline d\) from \(\texttt{def:endpoint-extension}\) with \(\sup_{Y\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R(D,\overline d;Y)\le\max_{Y\in\mathcal M\cap\{0,1\}^{2KN}}\mathcal R(D,d;Y)\). Moreover, invariant procedures and priors reduce the unrestricted game exactly to \(\operatorname{val}(\mathsf P)=\operatorname{val}(\mathsf Q)=R^\star\), with rational kernel \(H\), attainment, a posterior-mean endpoint rule on positive-mass cells, arbitrary clipped values on zero-mass cells, and an implementable correlated design obtained from assignment histograms followed by the conditional uniform sampling of \(\texttt{lem:conditional-uniformity}\). The orbit data have at most \((m+1)^{O(2^{2Kb}+K2^b)}\) entries.
statements.justification: This is the lossless finite reduction for every feasible exact-count menu, including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus, while retaining the full observation hypergraph.
statements.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 and Hull2026 obtain endpoint reductions for no interference, while KandirosHarshawSavje2026 bounds a graph-indexed network game; none gives an exact polynomial-size orbit game for a non-pairwise exact-count observation hypergraph.
statements.consumer: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018's saturation shares can be chosen against exact bounded-schedule risk while simultaneously selecting a nonlinear analysis rule.

statements.statement: For \(K=2\), a size-three cluster, and \(r_{3,1}=1\), the three label-one control-exposure coordinates are pairwise jointly observable but are not jointly observable as a triple. Hence no pairwise conflict graph has independent sets equal to the feasible observation sets of this exact-count experiment, whereas \(H\) retains the correct triple obstruction.
statements.justification: The proposition identifies the first combinatorial obstruction that a graph surrogate deletes.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Proposition 2.2, characterizes its arbitrary-neighborhood-interference experiment through a pairwise conflict graph; the exact-count saturation channel has higher-order feasibility constraints.
statements.consumer: Certificate builders can reject graph-based kernels before they generate invalid risks or designs for fixed-count saturation trials.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(K\) and \(b\), every rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary entries and menus constant in \(a\), every rational contrast \(c\), and every size profile \(s\), does the handle \(\mathfrak C\) admit a complete Turing-model proof that constructs the exact rational orbit kernel, weakly optimizes \(\mathsf P\) and \(\mathsf Q\), and returns in time polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size, the rational input bit length, and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) a rational design, endpoint estimator table, and least-favorable prior with directly checkable bounds \(\underline R\le R^\star\le\overline R\) and \(\overline R-\underline R\le\varepsilon\), together with a total continuous-outcome decoder on every zero-probability face?
statements.justification: The general finite conic game is not yet implementable until coefficient growth, weak optimization, outward rounding, and zero-face decoding are controlled in bits even for boundary or label-constant menus.
statements.gap: Kallus2021 establishes mixed-strategy optimality without a bit-certified exact orbit compiler, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 gives a polynomial approximation for a different graph design while conjecturing hardness of its full game.
statements.consumer: An experimental team can archive a machine-checkable risk interval and a deployable randomization-and-analysis protocol instead of an unaudited floating-point optimum.

statements.statement: For every feasible treated-count table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary counts and menus constant in \(a\), the equality \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}=R^\star\) holds if and only if the finite system in \(\texttt{def:independence-feasibility-system}\) is feasible. At every feasible solution, all assignment orbits with positive independent-design mass attain the common dual value, and every positive-likelihood observation cell uses the posterior-mean decision specified in \(\texttt{def:dual-game}\); zero-likelihood cells may take any value in \([-L,L]\).
statements.justification: This gives an exact, finite answer to when common-probability independent saturation loses nothing.
statements.gap: Hull2026 proves independence minimaxity under no interference, while CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 compares saturation dispersion for a difference-in-means estimator under a linear interference model; neither gives an if-and-only-if frontier for unrestricted estimators under exact-count interference.
statements.consumer: A trial planner can test whether ordinary independent cluster saturation is certified minimax before adopting a correlated mechanism.

statements.statement: For two size-three clusters, \(K=2\), \(r_{3,1}=1\), \(r_{3,2}=2\), and coefficient order \((c_{1,1},c_{0,1},c_{1,2},c_{0,2})=(3,-1,-1,-1)\), a rational 78-decision procedure and a 17-orbit prior certify \(1.3649753<R^\star\le1.364981422\) with primal-dual gap below \(10^{-5}\), while a 15-orbit prior certifies \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}>1.3659\). Thus \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}-R^\star>0.000918578\). For every rational \(t\) with \(|t|\le10^{-5}\), replacing \(c\) by \((3+t,-1-t,-1,-1)\) preserves \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}-R^\star>7\times10^{-4}\).
statements.justification: The rational separation proves that cross-cluster correlation can lower unrestricted minimax risk, not merely the variance of a selected linear estimator.
statements.gap: Hull2026's independent-design theorem relies on a no-interference tensorization, and CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 optimizes a conventional estimator; the certified saturation instance permits every measurable estimator on both sides.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a concrete reason for BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018-style trials to consider correlated saturation labels when robust finite-population MSE is the design criterion.

statements.statement: For \(K=2\), \(s_g=3\) for every \(g\), \(r_{3,1}=1\), \(r_{3,2}=2\), and \((c_{1,1},c_{0,1},c_{1,2},c_{0,2})=(1,-1,-1,1)\), independent cluster labels with common probability \(1/2\) are minimax and \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}=R^\star\) for every \(m\), because the label-complement action is transitive on local assignments and preserves the target.
statements.justification: A nondegenerate equality regime is a required sanity check on the strict-separation mechanism.
statements.gap: The closest unrestricted no-interference results establish independence generally; this proposition isolates the saturation symmetry under which that benchmark survives interference.
statements.consumer: Designers with complement-symmetric direct-and-saturation objectives can retain an ordinary independent implementation without sacrificing worst-case risk.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite population is partitioned into \(m\) labeled clusters; the chosen law \(D\) randomizes jointly over cluster saturation labels and exact treated subsets.
sampling_model.units: Potential outcomes \(Y_{g i}(z,a)\) are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: Cluster \(g\) receives label \(A_g\), then exactly \(r_{s_g,A_g}\) of its \(s_g\) units are treated.
sampling_model.overlap: The general results allow every feasible count \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus. Interiority is imposed only for the stated forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes; saturation variation is imposed only for the last two. Optimal designs may assign zero probability to labels or assignment orbits.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the estimator is chosen jointly with the randomization and may be nonlinear in the revealed outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives standard errors and power criteria for individual saturation and slope effects under a clustered regression model.
Theorem 1 shows that independent fair assignment with a nonlinear estimator is minimax over bounded no-interference potential outcomes.
Theorem 2.3 Bernoulli-lifts the binary no-interference minimax experiment to bounded outcomes and decodes a nonlinear rule.
Proposition 2.2 expresses the arbitrary-neighborhood-interference minimax risk as a function of a pairwise conflict graph.
The paper optimizes bias and variance of the difference-in-means estimator across randomized saturation designs under a linear interference model.
Theorem 2.1 proves minimax complete randomization by group averaging under permutation invariance for a fixed invariant estimator.

tldr: Randomized saturation experiments expose overlapping vectors of own-treatment-by-saturation responses, so their unrestricted design-and-estimation problem is neither the no-interference tensor product nor a pairwise conflict-graph game. For fixed saturation count and bounded cluster size, every feasible treated-count table, including boundary counts and a constant treated-count menu, admits an exact reduction of worst-case mean squared error over all correlated designs, bounded schedules, and measurable estimators to a rational endpoint orbit game. Conditional uniform subset randomization is without loss, and independent-saturation minimaxity has a finite primal-dual characterization. Interiority is confined to the forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes, while saturation variation is confined to the last two; the rational two-cluster, size-three certificate gives a strict correlated-saturation advantage on an infinite rational contrast neighborhood. The central open task is a complete polynomial Turing bit-complexity proof, including coefficient construction, weak conic optimization, outward-rounded certificates, and total nonlinear-estimator decoding on zero-mass faces.

project_justification.gap: Saturation-design papers optimize power or the bias and variance of specified regression or inverse-probability estimators, while recent unrestricted minimax papers either assume no interference or replace observation feasibility by a pairwise conflict graph. None preserves the exact-count observation hypergraph while jointly optimizing the first-stage law and an arbitrary measurable estimator across the full feasible menu, including zero, full, and label-constant treated counts.
project_justification.niche: Fixed saturation-label count and bounded cluster size leave exponentially many labeled schedules but only polynomially many size-tagged response, assignment, and observation histograms, whether treated counts are interior, on the boundary, or constant across labels. That symmetry permits an exact decision-theoretic quotient without assuming independence or linearity.
project_justification.fill: The paper establishes endpoint completeness and a stabilizer-weighted rational primal-dual orbit game for every feasible count table, with implementable correlated randomization and nonlinear estimation; it then gives a general finite independent-design frontier, confines interiority to the higher-order obstruction, equality witness, and strict rational separation certificate, and confines saturation variation to the last two, while exposing bit complexity and zero-face decoding as the open task.

related_work: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 supplies the application-facing direct and spillover design tradeoff, but its Theorem 1 optimizes regression-based precision rather than unrestricted bounded-schedule risk; the general orbit result also covers pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant exact-count menus. HudgensHalloran2008 and JiangImaiMalani2023 establish randomization-based estimands, unbiased estimators, variances, and inference for two-stage designs; they do not choose a minimax nonlinear procedure. AronowSamii2017 gives the design--exposure--estimand factorization and exact joint exposure-probability bookkeeping used to define the observation channel. BasseFeller2018 makes unequal cluster sizes and person-versus-cluster weighting explicit. Bai2023 and Kallus2021 motivate group symmetrization and mixed designs, but do not construct the saturation response kernel or certify its bit complexity. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 solve closely related unrestricted bounded no-interference games; their independence conclusion depends on a tensorized observation channel. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies unrestricted network-experiment minimax risk through a pairwise conflict graph, whereas Theorem 2 proves that the interior size-three fixed-count slice has an irreducible triple obstruction. CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 shows that interference changes desirable saturation dispersion under a linear model and fixed estimator; Theorems 3 and 4 instead compare independent and correlated label laws while allowing every measurable estimator. Interiority is confined to the obstruction, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry instances, and saturation variation to the latter two.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact arithmetic verifier confirms the 78-decision upper procedure, the 17-orbit unrestricted lower certificate, the 15-orbit independent lower certificate, and all 333,336 binary response orbits. A separate labeled enumeration for cluster sizes \((3,3,4)\) matches the size-tagged orbit kernel and normalizes to one for all six assignment histograms under the checked treated-count table. These are presolve diagnostics, not proofs of the general orbit theorem or the Turing bit bound.
honest_scope: Endpoint completeness, finite minimax duality, the orbit formulas, and conditional uniformity hold for every feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary counts and menus constant across labels. The finite independence criterion has the same general scope. Interiority is used only for the forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes, and saturation variation only for the last two. The full Turing bit-complexity and total zero-face decoder are exposed in \(\texttt{oeq:bit-certified-compiler}\) as the first-class open content. The paper does not claim an elementary closed-form classification of the independence frontier, a separation with the number of clusters tending to infinity, or exact rational optimizers. The complement-symmetry proposition supplies the required equality reduction.

seed_details.seed: Exact endpoint observation-hypergraph orbit game for bounded randomized saturation experiments
seed_details.anchor: SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026, Theorems 2.2--2.3 and Appendix A; BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018, Sections 2.2, 3.1, 4, and 5
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the no-interference scalar count reduction by a likelihood kernel on complete response, assignment, and observation-hypergraph orbits.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from bounded-outcome Bernoulli lifting and finite minimax duality in SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026.
seed_details.rebuttal: The lift supplies only endpoint completeness; exact-count interference requires a new non-pairwise kernel, stabilizer weights, correlated design actions, and total decoding.

seed_details.seed: Bit-certified polynomial orbit compiler with rational epsilon saddles and zero-face decoding
seed_details.anchor: Kallus2021, mixed-strategy design formulation and conclusion; prior proposal \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\), specialization \(v1\), technical limitation
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace existential group averaging and real-arithmetic conic optimization by canonical histogram enumeration with explicit rational stabilizer multiplicities and facial reduction.
seed_details.red_team: Routine application of polynomial-time second-order-cone programming once the finite game is written.
seed_details.rebuttal: The program itself must be built without labeled enumeration, its coefficients have growing bit length, and zero-mass perspectives require certified facial treatment and total estimator recovery.
seed_details.disposition: selected as the first-class open question

seed_details.rebuttal: The exact-count observation hypergraph does not tensorize; exact rational priors certify a strict gap that persists on a rational contrast neighborhood.

literature_map: The application thread runs from HudgensHalloran2008's fixed-count two-stage direct and spillover estimands through BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018's regression-power allocation problem, BasseFeller2018's unequal-size weighting, and JiangImaiMalani2023's unbiased randomization inference. The exposure thread is AronowSamii2017's exact design--exposure kernel. The minimax thread is Kallus2021 and Bai2023 on mixed designs and invariance, Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 on unrestricted nonlinear bounded-outcome procedures without interference, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 on graph-based network minimax bounds. CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 confirms that interference changes the preferred saturation distribution but fixes a model and estimator. No inspected source contains the exact size-tagged hypergraph orbit equality, the zero-face rational compiler, or the unrestricted correlated-versus-independent saddle frontier.
novelty_justification: The closest all-procedure results are Hull2026, Theorem 1, and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026, Theorems 2.2--2.3; both exploit a no-interference observation channel and conclude that independent assignment is minimax. The closest interference result is KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Proposition 2.2, whose pairwise conflict graph cannot encode the minimal forbidden triple created by an interior size-three exact-count saturation slice. The proposed kernel preserves that higher-order observation structure and remains exact for every feasible treated-count table, including boundary and label-constant menus; it admits correlated saturation actions and yields an exact finite conic equality rather than rate bounds. The rational witness then proves a strict reversal of the no-interference independence conclusion even after optimizing over every measurable estimator, and continuity promotes it from one hand-tuned contrast to an infinite rational neighborhood.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: For finite-population two-stage randomized saturation experiments, fix saturation-label count K, cluster-size bound b, rational treated-count table, and a rational direct/saturation contrast over bounded own-treatment-by-saturation potential outcomes. Allow arbitrary joint laws over saturation labels and feasible treated subsets and arbitrary measurable estimators. Prove endpoint completeness by an explicit multilinear extension, derive a polynomial-size rational convex primal/dual orbit game for fixed K,b with implementable optimal correlated design and nonlinear estimator, and extract rational epsilon-saddle certificates including all zero-probability faces. Prove uniform conditional subset randomization is without loss, give the finite primal-dual feasibility characterization of when optimized common-probability independent saturation is minimax, and prove a strict correlated-saturation advantage for the certified two-size-three-cluster instance and its infinite rational contrast neighborhood. Preserve the actual exact-count observation hypergraph rather than replacing it by a pairwise conflict graph, and do not claim an elementary closed-form equality classification, growing-cluster separation, or exact rational optimizers. The applied consumer is Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--Ozler's randomized-saturation design and its direct/spillover analysis.
